conceptual assets.information: The operational enable state determines whether the one-wire controller, its FIFOs, and the generated clock request are active. The IP uses it to enable operation and to clear the FIFOs when disabled.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the enable state at line 142 and the state controls operation and the clock-enable output at lines 258-273; availability is at risk because disabling it clears both FIFOs and stops clock ticks at lines 199, 231, and 258-263.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized control-register write could disable the controller, clear queued data, and withhold the clock-enable output.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and divider settings determine the rate at which one-wire transfer steps are paced. One-wire operation depends on these settings to generate the internal transfer ticks.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes set the prescaler and divider at lines 144-145 and they control tick generation at lines 260-265; availability is at risk because an altered rate can prevent or stall serial progress through the tick-dependent logic at lines 360-367.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized timing-setting write could make one-wire transfers run at an invalid rate or stop progressing.

conceptual assets.information: The clear control requests removal of queued transmit and receive information. The controller uses it to clear both FIFO instances.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write sets the clear control at line 143 and it clears both FIFOs at lines 199 and 231; availability is at risk because asserting it discards pending commands and received results at those same lines.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized clear command could erase queued commands or received data and disrupt an in-progress transfer.

conceptual assets.information: The command selects the one-wire operation, such as bit transfer, byte transfer, reset, or no operation. The serial engine decodes it to select the transaction sequence.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the bus writes the command into the transmit FIFO at line 201 and the serial engine decodes it at lines 323-335; availability is at risk because the decoded command determines whether and which transaction sequence runs at lines 331-335.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized transmit-FIFO write could replace a requested operation with a reset, no-op, or different transfer type.

conceptual assets.information: The payload byte written by software is transmitted over the one-wire interface. The serial engine uses it while generating the one-wire output waveform.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because bus data enters the transmit path at line 201 and influences the externally observable one-wire output at lines 300-302; integrity is at risk because an unauthorized write can replace the payload before it is loaded for serial transmission at line 328 and used by the output-control logic at line 342.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read or alter a payload supplied for transmission, exposing it on the one-wire line or causing a wrong device command or data value.

conceptual assets.information: The sampled one-wire bits form a received data byte that is queued for software to read. The IP depends on it to return data received from the one-wire device.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because sampled one-wire data enters at line 296 and is returned through the bus readback at line 161; integrity is at risk because the sampled value is assembled into the receive word at line 232 and an altered input or stored result changes the returned byte.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the receive readback or spoof the sampled one-wire bits so software receives an incorrect byte.

conceptual assets.information: The presence result records whether a one-wire device responded during reset detection. Software reads it together with the received result word to determine device presence.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the result is computed from the sampled line at line 375, placed in the receive word at line 232, and returned in the response at line 162.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could spoof the one-wire presence sample or corrupt the stored result so software falsely detects or misses a device.

conceptual assets.information: The sensed one-wire level is exposed as a software-readable status value. It supports observing the current sampled state of the one-wire interface.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the one-wire level is sampled into the sense path at line 296 and returned through the status readback at line 158, so alteration can falsify the reported line state.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could falsify the sensed line status and cause software to make an incorrect decision about the one-wire bus.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt request signals that the controller is enabled, transmit work is not queued, and the serial engine is idle. The integrating system can depend on it to service the controller.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because irq_o is produced from the enable, transmit availability, and busy state at line 243 and can therefore report a false service condition; availability is at risk because withholding irq_o can prevent the integrating system from servicing the controller.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the interrupt request to be suppressed or asserted at the wrong time, delaying service or causing incorrect host handling.
